messages.author: b63f60d8e029eb83
messages.subject: Convergence issue: Mplus and Lavaan
parts:
Hey Everyone,

I am learning R through duplicating output from past studies conducted on Mplus. I am having an odd issue where a particular CFA model from a data set will converge in Mplus but not in Lavaan.

Here is my syntax:
#importing the data
data1 <- read.table("C:\\Users\\Steven\\Desktop\\kc_rational.csv", header=TRUE, sep=",")

data1 <- data1[!(data1$age == 9),]

#turning missing data (9) into NA
data1[data1==9] <- NA

#creating variables
#I am sure there is a better way to do this
i84 <- data1$i84
i105 <- data1$i105
i160 <- data1$i160
i412 <- data1$i412
i431 <- data1$i431
i264 <- data1$i264
ri429 <- data1$ri429
i487 <- data1$i487
i489 <- data1$i489
i511 <- data1$i511
i21 <- data1$i21
ri83 <- data1$ri83
i202 <- data1$i202
i379 <- data1$i379
ri455 <- data1$ri455
ri34 <- data1$ri34
i240 <- data1$i240
ri266 <- data1$ri266
i548 <- data1$i548
i35 <- data1$i35
i540 <- data1$i540
age <- data1$age
gender <- data1$rgender

model1 <- '
#sp = school problems
sp =~ i84 + i105 + ri160 + i412 + i431
#sa = substance abuse
sa =~ i264 + ri429 + i487 + i489 + i511
#fp = family problems
fp =~ i21 + ri83 + i202 + i379 + ri455
#vsn = violation of social norms
vsn =~ ri34 + i240 + ri266 + i548 + i35 + i540
#Regressing on
sp ~ age + gender
sa ~ age + gender
fp ~ age + gender
vsn ~ age + gender
'

#creating the fit stat
fit1 <- cfa(model1, data = data1, estimator = "WLSMV", mimic = "Mplus", ordered = c("i84", "i105", "ri160", "i412",
       "i431", "i264", "ri429", "i487", "i489", "i511", "i21", "ri83",
       "i202", "i379", "ri455", "ri34", "i240", "ri266", "i548", "i35", "i540"))

summary(fit1, fit.measures = TRUE)

Verbose tells me the model stops after 19 iterations due to "False Convergence (8)". My hunch is it has something to do with nlminb and its default settings.

Is there a way to set nlminb parameters to mimic what Mplus uses?

Attached is a csv of the data set and the Mplus output I am working from. Thank you in advance for your help.

Steven Hirsch
PhD Student @ Central Michigan University

You can skip all of this:

> #I am sure there is a better way to do this
> i84 <- data1$i84
> i105 <- data1$i105
> i160 <- data1$i160
> i412 <- data1$i412
> i431 <- data1$i431
> i264 <- data1$i264
> ri429 <- data1$ri429
> i487 <- data1$i487
> i489 <- data1$i489
> i511 <- data1$i511
> i21 <- data1$i21
> ri83 <- data1$ri83
> i202 <- data1$i202
> i379 <- data1$i379
> ri455 <- data1$ri455
> ri34 <- data1$ri34
> i240 <- data1$i240
> ri266 <- data1$ri266
> i548 <- data1$i548
> i35 <- data1$i35
> i540 <- data1$i540
> age <- data1$age
> gender <- data1$rgender
because lavaan will find the variables names in your data.frame (mydata).

> model1 <- '
> #sp = school problems
> sp =~ i84 + i105 + ri160 + i412 + i431
> #sa = substance abuse
> sa =~ i264 + ri429 + i487 + i489 + i511
> #fp = family problems
> fp =~ i21 + ri83 + i202 + i379 + ri455
> #vsn = violation of social norms
> vsn =~ ri34 + i240 + ri266 + i548 + i35 + i540
> #Regressing on
> sp ~ age + gender
> sa ~ age + gender
> fp ~ age + gender
> vsn ~ age + gender
> '
>
> #creating the fit stat
> fit1 <- cfa(model1, data = data1, estimator = "WLSMV", mimic = "Mplus",
> ordered = c("i84", "i105", "ri160", "i412",
> "i431", "i264", "ri429", "i487", "i489", "i511", "i21", "ri83",
> "i202", "i379", "ri455", "ri34", "i240", "ri266", "i548", "i35",
> "i540"))
>
> summary(fit1, fit.measures = TRUE)
>
> Verbose tells me the model stops after 19 iterations due to "False
> Convergence (8)". My hunch is it has something to do with nlminb and its
> default settings.
> Is there a way to set nlminb parameters to mimic what Mplus uses?

Not really. But one thing you could try is to run a few 'Nelder Mead'
simplex iterations before we let nlminb kick in:

fit1 <- cfa(model1, data = data1, estimator = "WLSMV", mimic = "Mplus",
ordered = c("i84", "i105", "ri160", "i412",

"i35", "i540"), control=list(init_nelder_mead=TRUE), verbose = TRUE)

which seems to convergence. If the fit measures are not the same, we
would need to inspect if the sample statistics are the same, and if the
same number of parameters are used in both software packages.

Yves.
